subject: Midpoint OKR posture: proposed re-scope, tradeoffs & dependency asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Paige Lee <paige@atlashealth.com>
Cc: CloudScale Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midpoint: OKR posture & proposed re-scope for latency objective

Hi all —

Quick mid-point check on the "Reduce 95th pct latency" OKR (Q3). This thread is to surface current posture, propose a pragmatic re-scope for the QBR readout, and collect dependency commitments so we have clear owners going into the exec review. I attached an initial rebaseline spreadsheet (okr_rebaseline.xlsx) and a first-pass QBR slide (qbr_slide_draft.pdf).

Current status (brief):
- Baseline: 95th request latency reduced ~18% vs. baseline in private tests; production cohorts showing ~12% with high variance during peak.
- Root causes: a) GPU oversubscription on the private pool during bursts, b) higher-than-expected seq lengths from the Atlas pilot, c) model-level memory pressure causing occasional spill to CPU.

Proposal (recommended):
- Re-scope the Q3 latency target from 30% -> 20% reduction at 95th for the initial beta cohort, with a clearly documented plan to recover to 30% by end of Q4. This preserves a credible delivery commitment while removing an operational blocker that would otherwise risk sustained SLA misses.

Concrete asks (please reply with owner + ETA):
1) Vivek — confirm Dedicated capacity lead time (region: us-west) and cost uplift for reserving 2x A100-class GPUs for the beta lanes; if Dedicated not feasible, list alternatives (e.g., burst-only pool, preemptible blenders).
2) Vivek — can we run a 2-week mixed-precision + autotune experiment on the Atlas subset (test flag + telemetry capture)? Need a short spec for SRE to enable.
3) Naomi — can you craft a 1-slide executive summary that frames the re-scope and the recovery plan (two bullets: why we re-scoped, how we get back on track)? Deadline: EOD Wed so I can fold into the QBR deck.
4) Paige/Atlas — can you confirm acceptance of a temporary 20% target for the beta cohort and whether you need any specific telemetry or compliance evidence to feel comfortable with that shift?
5) Procurement/CloudScale — please standby for a short procurement request if Dedicated capacity is approved.

Risks: if we keep 30% as firm for the QBR, we should expect to call out a contingency ask (credits / extended SLA) which will slow negotiations. Goal is transparency and a united ask to execs.

Thanks,
Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Paige Lee <paige@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Midpoint: OKR posture & proposed re-scope for latency objective

Thanks for the clear write-up, Hannah. Quick responses inline below.

Dedicated capacity (us-west): realistic lead time for a committed 2x A100 config is ~6 weeks from signed order (procurement + capacity reservation + networking). Cost uplift ballpark: ~+35% on top of current variable run cost — I'll push exact numbers to procurement (CC'd). If 6 weeks is too long, options:
- Short-term: carve out a reserved burst pool (we can schedule capacity windows for Atlas traffic) — low lead time but higher per-hour cost.
- Medium-term: optimize model runtime (quantization + mixed precision + kernel autotune).

Experiment ask: we can run a 2-week mixed-precision + autotune experiment. Requirements from my side: a clear experiment cohort (please confirm sample IDs for Atlas), expected SLOs for the test (latency target, acceptable error delta), and tagging for telemetry. I can have a run spec by Thu EOD. I'll need SRE time to enable the test flag and capture KV/cache metrics.

Tradeoff suggestion: try the experiment first while procurement processes Dedicated; if the experiment shows >18% improvement in production-like traffic, we may not need full Dedicated immediately. If it only nets +5–10%, we'll escalate with procurement.

I'll follow up in procurement thread with the cost worksheet.

-Vivek
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Paige Lee <paige@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint: OKR posture & proposed re-scope for latency objective

Hannah — draft executive summary for QBR below (feel free to copy verbatim into slide):

"Mid-quarter posture: We are re-targeting the 95th percentile latency improvement from 30% to 20% for the Q3 beta cohort. This adjustment preserves predictable availability while enabling targeted runtime experiments and a capacity request that together form a clear path back to the 30% goal by Q4. Next steps: 1) Run a 2-week mixed-precision + autotune experiment (owner: Serving Runtime), 2) Reserve short-term Dedicated capacity if experiment results are insufficient (owner: Procurement/Platform)."

Suggested one-line callout for execs: "Re-scope reduces near-term risk while preserving our long-term performance ambition; customer pilot (Atlas) has accepted the temporary adjustment."

Deadline: I can finalize this into your slide by EOD Wed if you confirm the phrasing.

-Naomi
VP, Customer Success (exec readout)

From: Paige Lee <paige@atlashealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint: OKR posture & proposed re-scope for latency objective

Thanks for the transparency — Atlas has reviewed the data and for the beta cohort we are OK with the temporary 20% 95th-target. We prefer that this is timeboxed (explicit recovery plan to 30% by end of Q4).

Requests from our side:
- Weekly 30-minute sync for the pilot team (invite to follow)
- Access to the KV/cache telemetry you mentioned (read-only view or scheduled exports)
- Confirmation of any compliance artifacts we need to sign off on (SOC2 evidence, data retention notes)

We appreciate the tradeoff approach.

—Paige
Head of Product, Atlas Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Paige Lee <paige@atlashealth.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Midpoint: OKR posture & proposed re-scope for latency objective

Thanks, everyone — consolidating owners and deadlines below so this is actionable for the QBR prep: 

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Vivek: procurement worksheet + committed cost estimate for 2x A100 in us-west; note alternatives. ETA: Fri 08/07 COB.
- Vivek: experiment spec for 2-week mixed-precision + autotune (includes sample IDs and telemetry tags for SRE). ETA: Thu 08/05 EOD.
- Naomi: 1-slide exec summary + one-line callout finalized. ETA: Wed 08/05 EOD.
- Hannah: fold Naomi's slide into the QBR deck and annotate risks/ask. ETA: Thu 08/06 noon.
- Paige/Atlas: confirm access method for KV/cache telemetry and accept weekly sync invite (Paige). ETA: Tue 08/04 EOD.
- Procurement/CloudScale: standby for formal request — procurement lead will be looped once Vivek posts the worksheet.

I'll send a short invite for a 30-min pilot sync (first meeting Thu 08/06) and attach the rebaseline spreadsheet to the calendar. If anything above shifts, flag immediately so we can adjust the QBR slide.

Forwarding the earlier notes for context.

Thanks,
Hannah
--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
